surfaces.part: ramp surface descending away from the terrace lip (sand slope with faint step ridges)

answer.evidence: The tile fills the full 32x32 area with a uniform 32px width. It is a sand slope seen from above, with thin darker ridge lines at rows 6, 10, 14, 19 and 23 that mark steps. Lightness rises from L~177 at the top to L~210 at the bottom, so the ramp reads as descending. There is no vertical south face of 3 or more rows, no eave shadow and no ellipse. The dark 1-3px strips at the left and right edges from row 7 down are cliff-cut shading, not a receding side face. This is a flat top-down ramp surface with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a small bordered sand-coloured slab with a few horizontal grain lines. It looks like a plank or crate panel, not a 4x3-tile ground patch, and nothing shows the ramp descending between cliff walls. The measured facts are acceptable: 7 visible tones per tile (the paving reference also has 7, the grass 3), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the brown outline is tinted and reads as dark_material_tone. The weaknesses are structural. Only about 4 lightness steps carry the sand ramp, against 5-6 in Beodeul. There are no per-grain speckles, no scattered stones and no soil or sand grain texture. A uniform rim frames the whole piece like a sticker, where the references tile seamlessly. It also has no highlight-to-deep gradient to suggest a slope. A careful artist would not accept it beside the references.
